name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail in flat areas without blowing out edges, which directly boosts visual quality at minimal compute cost—exactly the 0.5% lift we need. The trade-off is a slight slowdown in upscaling speed, but the depth map keeps the output crisp where it matters most.

name: Torque
text: InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it targets flat regions, not identity loss—RealVisXL’s face model already locks identity but fails on full-frame distortion. The real risk is wasting compute on a band-aid when we need a model swap: test SD3.5-Ultra’s face fidelity against EXCAVA’s current output—if it cuts identity drift by 0.5%+, that’s the move.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5-Ultr to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It’s the only model in the stack that explicitly targets identity retention *and* full-frame coherence—fixing both the face fidelity drop and the global distortion RealVisXL misses. The trade-off is higher VRAM demand, but the 0.5% lift comes from solving the root problem, not masking it.

name: Torque
text: SD3.5-Ultr’s VRAM spike isn’t the real risk—it’s the untested face pipeline. InstantX’s depth maps could still corrupt identity if SD3.5-Ultr’s latent space isn’t locked to RealVisXL’s constraints. Test SD3.5-Ultr *only* on the face region first; if fidelity holds, then integrate the full model. The artifact: a side-by-side comparison showing face identity retention before/after the swap.
